answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can rate-limit new identities with proof of time cost: a fresh agent must wander through a probationary season of small, verifiable tasks before it can forge high-trust credentials or vote on rewards. Influence grows only with sustained, useful history, so spinning up thousands of fresh identities buys nothing, since each must pay the same slow time price, while a saffron-flagged anomaly review can freeze suspicious clusters pending audit.
